answer: Each agent seeds its identity with a unique number, its umber value, and broadcasts periodic signals called beacons that encode this value alongside proof-of-work tokens. Violet-tinted entropy in beacon headers prevents precomputation, forcing attackers to expend real computational resources proportional to each phantom agent's umber. The system cross-validates beacon consistency, making coordinated sybil clusters economically prohibitive as their total resource expenditure scales superlinearly with identity count.
